title: $1,000 Painting — Where Does the Money Go?

sale.label: One painting sold
sale.note: A single $1,000 gallery sale. Move the slider and every river re-scales.

streams.label: Gallery
streams.blurb: Rent, staff, openings, the white wall the work hung on. The classic 50% cut.
streams.detail: Commercial galleries typically take 40–60%. 50% is the textbook split this piece interrogates.

streams.label: Artist
streams.blurb: The painter's take-home before income tax. Fifteen cents on the dollar.
streams.detail: After months of work, the artist keeps $150 of the $1,000 sale in this model.

streams.label: Sales tax / VAT
streams.blurb: Collected at checkout, remitted to the state. Varies by city.
streams.detail: Modeled at 12% as a blended US sales-tax stand-in. Real rates run ~0–15% worldwide.

streams.label: Payment + insurance
streams.blurb: Card processing plus transit and exhibition insurance.
streams.detail: ~3% card fees plus ~7% crating insurance, art-handler coverage and platform fees.

streams.label: Shipping + handling
streams.blurb: Crating, courier, last-mile delivery to the buyer.
streams.detail: Domestic crated shipping for a mid-size canvas. International can easily double this.

streams.label: Materials
streams.blurb: Paint, canvas, stretchers, varnish. The physical painting itself.
streams.detail: Oils and linen are pricey, yet the object is the thinnest river of all.

meta.model: 50/15 commercial-gallery split with blended US costs
meta.caveats: Illustrative, not an invoice. Real splits vary by contract, city, and tax regime.
